noticias.titulo: 208 mil reproducciones · 41 mil reacciones | It’s not about race, it’s about ethnicity. I believe everyone should be able to have communities/countries of people of their own ethnic background that are for them. Nigerians get their own community. Indians get their own community. Chinese get their own community. And that means Germanic people, Nordic people, Celtic people etc. (white European ethnicities) also get their own place. They share a common language, common religion, a common culture, common values, and a common heritage. All “race” problems would be solved in a day if we organized in this way. Why is it racist to say all these other people can have their own place to live just for them with their own people and traditions, but if I want my own with my own people it’s an ethnostate? Because my skin is white? Being “white” does not even accurately represent all of the different cultures in European history, and my Germanic ethnicity is not the same as a Turkish ethnicity for example. I should have every right to a Germanic home that is for Germanic people just as much as the Indian has India, the Albanian has Albania, the Ghanaian has Ghana, or the Japanese has Japan. I want to live with and around people who have the same language, values, culture, and religion as me, not people who I have nothing in common with. Different cultures have different beauties about them that make them unique. I enjoy visiting them and learning about them. But they are not mine, and they never will be, and I do not want them in my home. | Will Witt

noticias.resumen: Scientists have discovered that the aging human brain may be far less isolated from the rest of the body than once believed. The finding overturns a long-standing assumption that these cells remain largely separate from the body’s immune system throughout life.

Hormone therapy use was linked to 39% lower odds of a dementia diagnosis and 35% lower odds of Alzheimer’s-related brain changes at autopsy, including amyloid plaques and tau tangles. Biomarker tests also suggested less amyloid buildup among hormone therapy users.

In early childhood, immune systems are still developing, leaving young children more vulnerable to serious illness. As children grow into their teenage years, booster doses help keep that protection strong and respond to new and emerging health risks. During pregnancy, vaccination plays a crucial role in protecting both parent and baby. Recommended vaccines help pass protective antibodies to babies before birth, giving them a safer start in life. In adulthood and older age, the immune system naturally becomes less robust. Vaccines help reduce the risk of severe illness and hospitalization, helping people stay healthy and live longer. Vaccination is about care, prevention and giving every generation the chance to learn, grow and thrive. #VaccinesWork | World Health Organization (WHO)

As children grow into their teenage years, booster doses help keep that protection strong and respond to new and emerging health risks. During pregnancy, vaccination plays a crucial role in protecting both parent and baby. Recommended vaccines help pass protective antibodies to babies before birth, giving them a safer start in life. In adulthood and older age, the immune system naturally becomes less robust. Vaccines help reduce the risk of severe illness and hospitalization, helping people stay healthy and live longer. Vaccination is about care, prevention and giving every generation the chance to learn, grow and thrive. #VaccinesWork | World Health Organization (WHO)

noticias.titulo: Copper's surprising melting behavior provides insights into future fusion design
noticias.resumen: Future fusion power plants aim to recreate the heart of a star here on Earth to power our future energy needs. While the core fusion plasma will burn at hundreds of millions of degrees, the surrounding structural components must handle sudden, punishing heat loads that rival the extreme temperatures faced by spacecraft upon reentry into Earth's atmosphere. Copper and its alloys are primary candidates for handling these intense heat fluctuations, making it vital to understand exactly how the metal behaves when pushed to its melting point.

The child was standing in their chair as the 6 August Porter Airlines flight taxied towards the runway, the airline said. Repeated attempts by an accompanying parent and crew to secure the child in their seat failed, so the crew elected to return to the terminal and have the two passengers disembark as “the aircraft could not take off in this unsafe condition”, it added…

Even people with severe language impairments caused by stroke were able to solve challenging logic puzzles as well as people without those impairments, while brain scans showed that language-processing regions stayed largely quiet during reasoning tasks.

Researchers warn that unusually hot oceans can fuel stronger storms, trigger harmful algal blooms, reduce seafood supplies, disrupt livelihoods, and contribute to anxiety, grief, and depression in coastal communities.

noticias.titulo: King Harold may have lost England by backing the wrong pope
noticias.resumen: A forgotten fragment of a lost papal letter is offering a surprising new explanation for the Norman Conquest. England may have backed the wrong pope during a bitter religious power struggle, giving Pope Alexander II a political reason to support William the Conqueror’s invasion. The discovery suggests Harold’s downfall in 1066 was shaped by intrigue in Rome as well as bloodshed at Hastings.

In just the past few weeks, media have reported that Puerto Rico is suffering a deep water crisis as severe drought has cut water supplies to thousands. Hungary’s only nuclear power plant is on the verge of shutting…

noticias.titulo: Syrian court sentences Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia for war crimes
noticias.resumen: Verdict relates to atrocities committed during the country’s 14-year civil war in which about 500,000 people died A Syrian court has sentenced the country’s former president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes during the 14-year civil war, in which about half a million people died. The two men fled to Moscow after being ousted by a lightning rebel offensive in December 2024 which toppled the dictatorial regime in just 11 days . Continue reading...

noticias.titulo: Black holes older than the Big Bang could explain dark matter
noticias.resumen: Some black holes roaming the Universe today may actually be older than the Big Bang. A new cosmic “bounce” model suggests the Universe expanded from an earlier contracting phase, allowing ancient black holes to survive the transition as cosmic fossils. These relics could potentially explain dark matter and why surprisingly massive objects appeared so early in cosmic history.

noticias.titulo: Scores dead in Colombia after powerful earthquake strikes west of country
noticias.resumen: Quake of 7.4 magnitude collapses and severely damages buildings in several major cities, including Cali and Pereira More than 100 people died after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, collapsing and severely damaging scores of buildings in major cities including Cali and Pereira. The US and Colombian geological surveys reported that a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck at 7.34am local time on Monday, with its epicentre in the western department of Chocó. It was felt in neighbouring Venezuela, still reeling from a deadly double earthquake on 24 June. Continue reading...

With this release, Kazakhstan became the first country to restore its tiger range after they had been thought extinct, with the last reliable sighting in the country recorded more than 70 years ago. noticias.titulo: NASA’s moon base is taking shape with 20+ lunar landings planned
noticias.resumen: NASA is assembling the foundations of a future Moon Base through a wave of robotic missions and powerful new commercial landers. More than 20 landings are planned through 2029, testing everything from precision landings and lunar communications to rovers, power systems, and technology that can survive the Moon’s extreme conditions. Upcoming missions could also make history by exploring the Moon’s far side and a mysterious magnetic lunar swirl. Each landing brings NASA closer to a sustained human presence on the lunar surface.

noticias.titulo: A simple blood test could detect multiple cancers and reveal where they started
noticias.resumen: UCLA researchers have created a blood test that can scan DNA signals for multiple cancers, liver diseases, and signs of organ damage—and even indicate where trouble may be developing. Early results suggest the inexpensive approach could bring medicine closer to a single blood test capable of catching a wide range of diseases before they become harder to treat.

noticias.titulo: The secret hidden in these ancient manuscripts isn’t written in ink
noticias.resumen: Researchers can now recover DNA from centuries-old parchment without damaging the manuscripts, turning historic documents into unexpected genetic time capsules. The hidden clues could reveal ancient trade routes, livestock history, manuscript origins, and details of everyday life stretching back more than a thousand years.

noticias.titulo: Exercise may help the aging brain “take out the trash”
noticias.resumen: Regular exercise may help the brain clear away harmful waste that can build up with age. Researchers found that physical activity supports several processes linked to the brain’s glymphatic cleanup system, including better sleep, lower inflammation, and healthier blood vessels. Because this waste-removal system becomes increasingly important as we get older, exercise could play a meaningful role in protecting against cognitive decline.

Police fired water cannon and teargas and swung batons as they tried to stop flag-waving demonstrators from clambering over barricades and surging towards the assembly in Ranchi, the state capital. noticias.titulo: New GLP-1 pill delivers up to 12% weight loss in 36 weeks
noticias.resumen: An experimental GLP-1 pill helped people with obesity or overweight lose as much as 12.1% of their body weight in just 36 weeks. Unlike injectable drugs such as Wegovy and Ozempic, aleniglipron is a small molecule that can be taken once daily with or without food and could potentially be produced more easily at scale.

noticias.titulo: Lion Nebula roars to life for Webb
noticias.resumen: Image: Observing across the starry 'plains' of space, the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope has taken images of NGC 2392, nicknamed the Lion Nebula. The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope previously viewed this planetary nebula in 2000, imaging the lion face-shaped target in visible light and revealing features such as the “mane” of hazy, comet-shaped objects. Now Webb has captured a clearer, more detailed view of the Lion Nebula due to its high-resolution imaging. At first glance the nebula’s overall structure in Webb’s infrared images, both with the NIRCam (Near Infrared Camera) and MIR…

noticias.titulo: 1 in 5 people may carry this hidden genetic heart risk
noticias.resumen: Very high levels of the inherited cholesterol-related particle Lp(a) were linked to a greater risk of major cardiovascular events, particularly stroke and cardiovascular death, in a study of more than 20,000 people. Since elevated Lp(a) often flies completely under the radar, a simple blood test could uncover hidden heart risk that standard cholesterol testing may miss.

noticias.titulo: Wildfires, drought and extreme heat, 2026
noticias.resumen: Earth observation satellites help us monitor phenomena such as wildfires, drought and heatwaves from space. This page is updated on a regular basis with a selection of ESA’s most recent news-related images showing how the effects of climate change are impacting our world.

noticias.titulo: Meta to open source its most powerful AI model as it takes swipe at OpenAI, Anthropic
noticias.resumen: Meta launched Muse Glimmer and plans to release Muse Spark 1.2 weights as Zuckerberg pushes for U.S. leadership in open AI.

noticias.titulo: Scientists discover a hidden switch inside silver nanocatalysts
noticias.resumen: Silver nanocatalysts have been found to switch where they perform their most important reactions depending on whether a solid oxide cell is making electricity or hydrogen. The discovery could enable smarter catalyst designs that boost clean power generation while making green hydrogen more energy-efficient.

noticias.titulo: La ONU ofrece apoyo a Colombia tras el terremoto de magnitud 7,4 que dejó más de 100 muertos
noticias.resumen: El sistema de Naciones Unidas sigue de cerca la emergencia y está preparado para apoyar la respuesta nacional. El potente sismo golpeó el oeste del país, provocó derrumbes y dejó personas atrapadas, mientras las autoridades continúan evaluando los daños y el número de víctimas.

noticias.titulo: Fighting deepens needs and fuels further displacement in Sudan
noticias.resumen: Ongoing conflict, displacement and funding shortages continue to deepen needs in Sudan, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned on Monday, underscoring the need for greater civilian protection.

noticias.titulo: Lebanon: UN peacekeepers count hundreds of Israeli strikes and incursions in a single weekend
noticias.resumen: Israeli forces fired 455 projectiles into south Lebanon and breached Lebanese airspace 97 times between Friday and Sunday, the UN's peacekeeping mission in the country reported Monday – among the heaviest fire seen in months.

noticias.titulo: UN offers support to Colombia after magnitude 7.4 earthquake kills dozens
noticias.resumen: The UN offered its support to Colombia on Monday after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck the west of the country, killing at least 111 people and injuring at least 87, including several children, while leaving others trapped under the rubble and causing landslides and serious damage to homes and infrastructure.

noticias.titulo: DR Congo: Ebola is killing people before they ever reach a doctor
noticias.resumen: More than 1,900 people have died in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak – and most of them never made it to a treatment centre. Between 60 and 70 per cent of deaths are happening in communities far from care, a gap that is now central to the World Health Organization's response.

noticias.titulo: Afghanistan: UN tells Taliban to open up on abuses committed by security forces
noticias.resumen: Five years into Taliban rule, Afghans still have almost no way of knowing whether soldiers, police and morality officers who abuse their power ever face consequences – and that secrecy is corroding trust in the State, the UN said Monday.

noticias.titulo: UN calls for urgent action to protect children from online information risks
noticias.resumen: More than eight in 10 young people aged 15 to 24 worldwide are now online, and in low-income countries they outpace the rest of the population nearly two to one.

noticias.titulo: Humanitarian aid warehouses come under attack in Ukraine
noticias.resumen: Russia’s ongoing full-scale invasion of Ukraine has left civilians vulnerable to repeated deadly attacks and humanitarian workers and key facilities being targeted and destroyed.

noticias.titulo: Expertos condenan la escalada de ataques contra palestinos en Gaza y Cisjordania
noticias.resumen: Un grupo de expertos en derechos humanos alertan del agudo deterioro de la situación en Palestina: 160 muertos en Gaza en julio y terror de colonos en Cisjordania. Denuncian que el genocidio continúa, la ayuda alimentaria no llega y las restricciones de movimiento son "instrumentos letales" que han costado la vida a un bebé y una mujer embarazada.

noticias.titulo: Equipos para elaborar productos cotidianos pueden terminar en la fabricación de drogas
noticias.resumen: Prensas para tabletas, reactores, mezcladoras y equipos de laboratorio tienen numerosos usos legítimos, pero también pueden terminar en instalaciones clandestinas. Un nuevo análisis identifica los puntos de la cadena comercial donde existe mayor riesgo de desvío.

noticias.titulo: Rusia destruye un almacén con suministros médicos en Ucrania
noticias.resumen: La agencia de salud logró trasladar parte de los suministros antes de que el edificio fuera destruido por completo. Los suministros estaban destinados a apoyar la atención médica de emergencia y mantener servicios esenciales en instalaciones sanitarias próximas a las zonas de combate.

noticias.titulo: Casi ningún país avanza al ritmo necesario para transformar sus sistemas alimentarios
noticias.resumen: La transformación de los sistemas alimentarios no depende solo de producir más comida. También exige dietas saludables, menor contaminación, mejores condiciones para quienes trabajan en el sector, instituciones más eficaces y una mayor capacidad para resistir crisis económicas y climáticas.

noticias.titulo: 240-million-year-old reptile fossil reveals a lost chapter before dinosaurs and crocodiles
noticias.resumen: A 240-million-year-old reptile discovered in Brazil is revealing what evolution looked like just before the rise of dinosaurs and crocodiles. The small predator had unusually positioned legs that may have allowed it to move more efficiently than many earlier reptiles. Its close relatives were previously known mostly from other continents, suggesting these ancient animals spread much farther across the Triassic world than scientists realized.

noticias.titulo: Potatoes may have given Indigenous Andeans a digestive superpower
noticias.resumen: The rise of the potato in the Andes appears to have left a lasting mark on human DNA. Indigenous Peruvians carry exceptionally high numbers of a starch-digestion gene, likely because people with more copies gained an evolutionary advantage once potatoes became a staple food. The change began thousands of years before European contact, providing unusually strong evidence that diet can shape human evolution.

noticias.titulo: The sun will vanish over Europe in a rare total solar eclipse: Watch live
noticias.resumen: A total solar eclipse will plunge parts of Europe into darkness on August 12, 2026, with Spain offering some of the best views. ESA will livestream the spectacle from the Javalambre Observatory, combining telescope feeds, drone footage, and expert commentary. At 20:31 CEST, the observatory will experience 1 minute and 21 seconds of totality, revealing the Sun’s normally hidden outer atmosphere.

noticias.titulo: El Gobierno puede poner condiciones a SAIC en Galicia para garantizar la seguridad nacional

noticias.titulo: Voyager 2 was running out of power. NASA just bought it more time
noticias.resumen: NASA engineers have found a clever way to squeeze more life out of Voyager 2, nearly half a century after it left Earth. In an operation nicknamed the “Big Bang,” the team simultaneously shut down certain power-hungry hardware and switched to lower-power alternatives while keeping the spacecraft warm enough to survive.

noticias.titulo: For 15,000 years, humans and dogs have been changing each other
noticias.resumen: Dogs have been shaping—and being shaped by—humans for about 15,000 years, evolving from early partners of hunter-gatherers into an astonishing range of specialized companions. Across the globe, they adapted alongside people to wildly different environments and needs, from powerful Arctic sled dogs and agile rainforest hunters to high-altitude dogs with genetic traits for surviving thin air. Some were even bred for wool, while others played important spiritual or ceremonial roles.

noticias.titulo: Cassini reveals a surprising twist in Saturn’s magnetic shield
noticias.resumen: Cassini data has revealed a surprising twist in Saturn’s magnetic shield: the planet’s rapid rotation appears to drag a key opening in its magnetosphere far toward the afternoon side instead of keeping it near noon, as happens on Earth. The finding confirms that giant planets like Saturn operate under a fundamentally different magnetic regime, where fast spin and charged material from moons such as Enceladus can overpower the Sun’s influence.
